record_under_review.evidence_span: Lit Silicon identifies thermally induced straggling coupled with concurrent computation and communication as a source of multi-GPU performance variation. The study proposes analytical performance and power models, detection and mitigation techniques, and evaluates three power-management strategies on two AMD Instinct MI300X systems, two workloads, and two LLM-training frameworks. It reports up to 6% performance and 4% power improvements.
record_under_review.hardware_or_process_assumptions: Single-node multi-GPU LLM training with concurrent computation and communication; evidence is specific to evaluated AMD MI300X systems and management policies.
record_under_review.limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; workload details, thermal traces, statistical variance, absolute energy, and the claimed datacenter cost implications require full-paper verification and broader hardware replication.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: Lit Silicon performance/power models, detection and mitigation techniques, and evaluation of TDP-constrained power optimization, node-level GPU power capping, and CPU power sloshing.
record_under_review.problem: Thermal imbalance across GPUs can create hotter, slower stragglers that slow cooler leader GPUs during overlapped computation and communication, reducing node-level efficiency.
record_under_review.title: Lit Silicon: A Case Where Thermal Imbalance Couples Concurrent Execution in Multiple GPUs
record_under_review.workload_or_benchmark: Two workloads on two AMD Instinct MI300X GPU systems using two LLM training frameworks.
